stories.summary: From 1 December, drivers commit an offence by holding a mobile device while their vehicle is moving, even if they are not using it. The same package creates a "purposeful endangerment" offence — deliberately using a vehicle to endanger life — carrying up to 15 years' jail and a lifetime driving ban, and raises maximum jail for dangerous driving causing grievous hurt to seven years for first offenders and 13 for repeat offenders.
stories.title: Holding a phone while driving becomes an offence from 1 December, even if you aren't using it
stories.why: The toughest road-safety overhaul in years, taking effect on Tuesday — it changes what every driver in Singapore can and cannot do behind the wheel.

stories.summary: Singapore says it is engaging with companies on exports, as the US chip curbs and reported Nvidia shipment halt put high-end chip access in question.
stories.title: Singapore says it is 'engaging' with firms on exports
stories.why: The government's live response to the chip-curbs story that directly affects Singapore's AI and data-centre sector.

stories.summary: Shipping giant CMA CGM is weighing trials of ethanol as a marine fuel bunkered in Singapore.
stories.title: CMA CGM weighs ethanol bunkering trials in Singapore
stories.why: Singapore is the world's largest bunkering port — a move to ethanol would be a notable step in the greening of shipping.

stories.summary: Cassidy Tan, 34, pleaded guilty to dangerous driving causing death after averaging 192km/h on the CTE in January 2024, killing motorcyclist Mohammad Oszaimi Osman. Prosecutors are seeking six-and-a-half years' jail and a 20-year driving ban; sentencing is set for 11 January 2027.
stories.title: Driver who averaged 192km/h pleads guilty over motorcyclist's death
stories.why: A high-profile fatal speeding case reaching its conclusion — days before the tougher 1 December road laws take effect.

stories.summary: A 21-year-old man was arrested for allegedly cheating two people through TikTok food orders.
stories.title: 21-year-old man arrested for allegedly cheating 2 individuals via TikTok food orders
stories.why: Food-order scams are reaching social commerce — a small case, but a warning about where scams are moving.

stories.summary: Bloomberg found export-restricted Blackwell chips — a GB300 NVL72 rack and a GB200 server — installed at a Shanghai data centre linked to Alice Huang and Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is under US investigation over alleged chip diversion. The gear was pledged as collateral for a 96 million yuan loan.
stories.title: Nvidia Blackwell chips turn up at China site tied to Alice Huang
stories.why: Hard evidence that the most advanced US chips reached China despite export controls — centred on a Singapore-linked firm.

stories.summary: OpenAI countersued Apple in a California federal court, accusing it of stealing trade secrets and pressuring hardware suppliers, in response to Apple's July lawsuit over its AI-device plans. Apple called the counterclaims a distraction from its own case.
stories.title: OpenAI countersues Apple for stealing trade secrets, FT reports
stories.why: The race to build AI hardware is now a courtroom fight between two giants, with supplier access at stake.

stories.summary: US stocks jumped in Friday's shortened post-Thanksgiving session — the Dow rose 1.2%, the S&P 500 1.6% and the Nasdaq 2.3% — capping the market's best week in over a year as investors piled back into beaten-down AI shares. The Nasdaq gained 6.7% on the week, its best in seven months.
stories.title: Wall Street ends higher as battered AI stocks gain in volatile week
stories.why: The AI sell-off that dominated November reversed sharply, setting the tone for December and for Asian markets on Monday.

stories.summary: Hackers breached the US Air Force's flagship Cloud One cloud platform, in a development that could jeopardise sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data. Cyber Command has been called in to assess the damage; application migrations have been paused and software updates blocked.
stories.title: Hackers breach US Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform
stories.why: A breach of a core US military cloud — with the hackers unidentified and the scope and any data stolen still unknown.

stories.summary: Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia, meeting in Islamabad under their Mecca defence pact, named Yemen's Houthis a threat to the kingdom for the first time and pledged to back Saudi security, while stressing diplomacy. No new troop deployments were decided.
stories.title: Houthis declared a 'threat' to S. Arabia
stories.why: The new trilateral pact is hardening into a real security bloc as Houthi attacks on Saudi targets escalate.

stories.summary: US forces used precision munitions to disable the propulsion of the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman after it tried to run the US blockade of Iran; the civilian crew was unharmed, US Central Command said.
stories.title: US military says it disabled commercial ship trying to run Iran blockade
stories.why: The US is now enforcing its Iran blockade with live fire against commercial shipping — a sharp escalation in the Gulf.

stories.summary: Indian drone and robotics startups are seeing surging military demand as geopolitics drives indigenisation, though they still face funding, testing and procurement hurdles.
stories.title: 'Nobody is going to help us': India's drone and robotics firms face hurdles amid growing military demand
stories.why: The drone revolution is reshaping defence industries well beyond the US and China.

stories.summary: Japan is considering a five-year defence plan worth about $350 billion — below what its military had sought, according to the Asahi newspaper.
stories.title: Japan eyeing $350 billion five-year defence plan, below military's wishes, Asahi reports
stories.why: The scale of Japan's rearmament, and the gap between what the military wants and what the government will fund, is a key regional signal.

stories.summary: Lithuania is confronting a growing Kremlin disinformation campaign, with Russian information operations against the Baltic state escalating.
stories.title: Lithuania confronts growing Kremlin disinformation
stories.why: Another frontline state reporting a step-up in Russian information operations — the pattern this category tracks.

tldr: Singapore: Tougher road laws from 1 Dec — holding a phone while driving becomes an offence, and using a car as a weapon can mean 15 years' jail.
Technology: Export-restricted Nvidia Blackwell chips found at a Shanghai data centre tied to Alice Huang and Singapore's Megaspeed.
Finance & global markets: Wall Street jumps in Friday's short session — the Nasdaq posts its best week in seven months as AI stocks rebound.
Defence & military: Hackers breach the US Air Force's flagship Cloud One platform; Cyber Command is called in.
Information warfare: Lithuania confronts a growing Kremlin disinformation campaign.
